sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **Class Relationships**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Association, aggregation, and composition
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **Class Relationships** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Association is a general relationship where one object uses or interacts with another
Aggregation (has-a) represents ownership where the part can exist independently
Composition (owns-a) is a strong aggregation where the part cannot exist without the whole
Multiplicity describes how many objects participate in a relationship (1, *, 0..1, etc.)
Class relationships are represented by different arrow types in UML diagrams

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Class Relationships - Association, aggregation, and composition. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: What is an 'association' between classes?
options: A general relationship where one class uses or interacts with another
A class that cannot be used with others
questions.explanation: Association is a general relationship where one class uses or interacts with another. For example, a Student class may be associated with a Course class.

questions.question: What is the difference between aggregation and composition?
options: In composition, the contained object cannot exist without the container; in aggregation, it can
Composition allows sharing objects, aggregation does not
questions.explanation: In composition, the contained object's lifecycle depends on the container (e.g., a Room cannot exist without a House). In aggregation, the contained object can exist independently (e.g., a Student can exist without a University).
